title: Local constructibility of containment of fibre associated points in an open subspace
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use chartwise local finite type and local finite presentation [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, with quasi-compact diagonal. A module of finite type is locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts; a finitely presented module has locally an exact presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to M\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Let $f:X\to Y$ be of finite presentation with $Y$ a scheme, let $M$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent module, and let $W\subseteq X$ be an open subspace such that $W\to Y$ is quasi-compact. Use the relative assassin on spaces [def-sfb-space-universal-relative-purity]: $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/Y}(M)$ is the union of the images of the fibrewise associated points on representable etale scheme charts, with scheme associated points as in [def-trf-relative-assassin]. Use the topology on space points [def-a1-space-point-topology] and constructible subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset]; a subset $E$ of a scheme $Y$ is locally constructible if every point of $Y$ has an affine open neighbourhood $V$ such that $E\cap V$ is a constructible subset of the topological space $|V|$. The subset $E=\{y\in Y\mid\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(M_y)\subseteq |W_y|\}$ is locally constructible in $Y$. Consequently, if $y\in Y$ and every generalization of $y$ belongs to $E$, there exists an open neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ such that $V\subseteq E$. A generalization $t$ of $y$ means $y\in\overline{\{t\}}$.

proof.text: Fix any affine open $B\subseteq Y$ and replace the family by $X_B\to B$, $M_B$ and $W_B$. Finite presentation of the morphism survives this base change, and $W_B\to B$ remains quasi-compact. The fibres over points of $B$ are the original fibres, by the fibre-product universal property. The affine scheme $B$ is qcqs, so finite presentation gives that $X_B$ is qcqs. It therefore suffices to show constructibility on this arbitrary affine base. In the next steps rename the restricted family $X\to B,M,W$.

source.place: Tag 0CVV, first affine-base reduction; finite-presentation base change and Tag 06G5.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale map $p:T\to X$ with $T$ affine. Both $T$ and $X$ are qcqs; hence the permanence theorem makes $p$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Etaleness gives local finite presentation: in any chart square $a:U\to T$, $b:V\to X$, $h:U\to V$ with $pa=bh$, the composite $pa:U\to X$ is representable etale, so the scheme map $h$ between two etale charts of $X$ is etale, hence locally of finite presentation. So $p$ is of finite presentation. Composition with $X\to B$ now makes $g:T\to B$ of finite presentation. Let $H=p^{-1}(W)$, an open subscheme of $T$. Since $W\to B$ is quasi-compact and $B$ is affine, $W$ is quasi-compact. Quasi-compactness of $p$, tested on the quasi-compact space $W$, makes $H$ quasi-compact. Since $B$ is quasi-separated, permanence makes $H\to B$ quasi-compact, which for this representable morphism of schemes is quasi-compactness in the scheme sense. These are precisely the hypotheses on the morphism and open needed for the scheme theorem.

source.place: Tag 0CVV, choice of affine surjective etale cover and verification for its inverse-image open; Tag 073B and Tag 03XQ.

proof.text: Put $N=p^*M$. Tensor pullback, being the specified left adjoint, preserves cokernel presentations and takes finite free terms to finite free terms. Thus a local finite presentation of $M$ gives one of $N$; this also justifies $M_B$ in step 1. Quasi-coherence follows directly from the local-presentation definition. The affine-chart calculus says that on the affine etale chart $T$, $N$ corresponds to its section module and that this module is finitely presented. Let $F$ be its associated quasi-coherent Zariski module; its finite module presentation sheafifies to a finite presentation of $F$. The etale--Zariski equivalence identifies $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $N$, and its pullback comparison identifies $(F_y)_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $N_y$ on every fibre. Thus the scheme associated points of these corresponding modules agree, since they are computed from the same Zariski module stalks.

source.place: Tag 0CVV, module on the affine chart; Tags 03LZ, 03M0, 03M1 (characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale, characterize-quasi-coherent, properties-quasi-coherent); Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), comparison with the Zariski module.

proof.text: For every $y\in B$, the atlas comparison gives $p_y(\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(N_y))=\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(M_y)$. Since $H_y=p_y^{-1}(W_y)$, inclusion of the right-hand set in $|W_y|$ is equivalent to inclusion of $\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(N_y)$ in $|H_y|$: each associated point upstairs maps into the displayed image, and each associated point downstairs has an associated lift. With step 3 this identifies $E\cap B$ with $\{y\in B\mid\operatorname{Ass}_{T_y}(F_y)\subseteq |H_y|\}$.

source.place: Tag 0CVV, equality of the fibrewise associated-point image and reduction of the containment condition.

proof.text: Apply the scheme constructibility theorem to $g:T\to B$, $F$ and $H$, whose hypotheses were checked in steps 2 and 3. It makes this last set constructible in $B$. Step 4 identifies it with $E\cap B$. As $B$ was an arbitrary affine open of $Y$, this proves the asserted local constructibility.

source.place: Tag 0CVV, final application of More on Morphisms Tag 05KR.

proof.text: Now fix $y\in Y$ all of whose generalizations belong to $E$, and choose an affine open $B$ containing $y$. The set $E_B=E\cap B$ is constructible by steps 1--5, and so is $C=B\setminus E_B$, since constructible subsets form a Boolean algebra. The affine scheme $B$ is qcqs and hence its point space is spectral. If $y\in\overline C^{B}$, apply the spectral closure-specialization theorem to the singleton family with sole member $C$. It gives $c\in C$ with $y\in\overline{\{c\}}^{B}$. The inclusion $B\hookrightarrow Y$ is continuous, so $c$ is also a generalization of $y$ in $Y$. The hypothesis puts $c$ in $E$, contradicting $c\in C$. Therefore $y\notin\overline C^{B}$.

source.place: Tag 05LW, constructible complement argument; Tag 0903 (lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed), part (1).

proof.text: Take $V=B\setminus\overline C^{B}$. It is open in $B$ and hence in $Y$, contains $y$, and is contained in $B\setminus C=E_B\subseteq E$ because $C\subseteq\overline C^{B}$. This proves the neighbourhood conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0CVV; Tag 05LW, with its closure step expressed using Tag 0903.

For a constructible complement on an affine scheme, a closure point is a specialization of a point of that complement; a generic spectral topology tool for the final neighbourhood assertion.

A scheme map between two representable etale charts of a space is etale; used to see that the representable etale atlas p is locally of finite presentation in the chart-test sense. Generic foundation on algebraic spaces, no node of the unit states it.

lean.statement: theorem fibreAssassinContainment_locallyConstructible {X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))} (Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace Y) (_hfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f.hom.hom)) (M : X.QCoh) (_hM : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation M.obj) (W : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (j : W ⟶ X) (_hj : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) j.hom.hom) (_hW : MapIsQuasiCompact (j.hom.hom ≫ f.hom.hom)) : (∀ y : Y.left, ∃ V : Y.left.Opens, y ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ Topology.IsConstructible ((Subtype.val : V → Y.left) ⁻¹' fibreAssassinContainmentLocus Y f M.obj (pointImage j.hom.hom))) ∧ (∀ y : Y.left, (∀ t : Y.left, y ∈ closure ({t} : Set Y.left) → t ∈ fibreAssassinContainmentLocus Y f M.obj (pointImage j.hom.hom)) → ∃ V : Y.left.Opens, y ∈ V ∧ (V : Set Y.left) ⊆ fibreAssassinContainmentLocus Y f M.obj (pointImage j.hom.hom))
